## Overview

This spec defines the byte format of the TLS handshake messages a TLS 1.3 and TLS 1.2 client and server exchange, as two functions:

- **decode_handshake** -- parses one complete handshake message (4-byte header and body) strictly and returns its fields, or the error that names the alert to send.
- **encode_handshake** -- serializes a message; `encode_handshake(decode_handshake(p, m)) == m` for every `m` that decodes.

It covers ClientHello, ServerHello and HelloRetryRequest, EncryptedExtensions, Certificate, CertificateRequest, CertificateVerify, Finished, NewSessionTicket, KeyUpdate, and the TLS 1.2 HelloRequest, ServerKeyExchange (ECDHE), ClientKeyExchange (ECDHE) and ServerHelloDone; and the extensions server_name, supported_groups, ec_point_formats, signature_algorithms,
application_layer_protocol_negotiation, extended_master_secret, supported_versions, cookie, key_share and renegotiation_info. Every other extension is carried as opaque bytes.

Semantic checks that need handshake state -- an extension the client did not offer, a group or suite that was not offered, a Finished of the wrong length -- belong to the `tls-handshake` and `tls12-handshake` specs.

**Out of scope:** reassembling messages from records, EndOfEarlyData, the PSK extensions' internal structure (pre_shared_key, psk_key_exchange_modes, early_data), certificate_authorities, oid_filters, status_request and signed_certificate_timestamp content, TLS 1.2 NewSessionTicket and CertificateStatus, RSA and DHE key exchange messages, and SSL 3.0 or TLS 1.0/1.1 formats.

## Types

### CodecError

```pseudocode
type CodecError =
  | DecodeError        // malformed: truncated, trailing bytes, a length out of its range, a bad value inside an extension
  | IllegalParameter   // well-formed but forbidden: duplicate extension, an extension not allowed in this message, KeyUpdate value, curve_type
  | UnexpectedMessage  // a message type not defined for the protocol
  | MissingExtension   // a TLS 1.3 CertificateRequest without signature_algorithms
```

Each is the alert of the same name (decode_error, illegal_parameter, unexpected_message, missing_extension).

### Protocols and message types

`protocol` is `"tls13"` or `"tls12"`. It decides which message types exist and the format of Certificate and CertificateRequest:

| Type | Message | `tls13` | `tls12` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | hello_request | | yes |
| 1 | client_hello | yes | yes |
| 2 | server_hello (and HelloRetryRequest) | yes | yes |
| 4 | new_session_ticket | yes | |
| 8 | encrypted_extensions | yes | |
| 11 | certificate | yes (1.3 format) | yes (1.2 format) |
| 12 | server_key_exchange | | yes |
| 13 | certificate_request | yes (1.3 format) | yes (1.2 format) |
| 14 | server_hello_done | | yes |
| 15 | certificate_verify | yes | yes |
| 16 | client_key_exchange | | yes |
| 20 | finished | yes | yes |
| 24 | key_update | yes | |

Any other type, including 5 (end_of_early_data) and 254 (message_hash), is `UnexpectedMessage`.

### HandshakeMessage

A decoded message is an object with `msg_type` and the fields below. Byte strings are `*_hex`; integers are numbers; `extensions` is a list of `Extension` in wire order, or `null` where the message may omit the block.

| `msg_type` | Fields |
|---|---|
| 1 | `legacy_version`, `random_hex` (32 bytes), `legacy_session_id_hex` (0 to 32 bytes), `cipher_suites` (list of uint16, non-empty), `legacy_compression_methods_hex` (1 to 255 bytes), `extensions` (list, or `null` when the message ends after the compression methods) |
| 2 | `legacy_version`, `random_hex`, `legacy_session_id_echo_hex` (0 to 32 bytes), `cipher_suite`, `legacy_compression_method`, `extensions` (list or `null`) |
| 8 | `extensions` |
| 11, `tls13` | `certificate_request_context_hex` (0 to 255 bytes), `certificate_list`: list of `{cert_data_hex (1 to 2^24-1 bytes), extensions}` |
| 11, `tls12` | `certificate_list`: list of `{cert_data_hex}` |
| 13, `tls13` | `certificate_request_context_hex`, `extensions` |
| 13, `tls12` | `certificate_types_hex` (1 to 255 bytes), `supported_signature_algorithms` (list of uint16, non-empty), `certificate_authorities_hex` (list of 1 to 65535-byte DER names) |
| 15 | `algorithm` (uint16 SignatureScheme), `signature_hex` (0 to 65535 bytes) |
| 20 | `verify_data_hex` (the whole body, any length) |
| 4 | `ticket_lifetime`, `ticket_age_add` (uint32), `ticket_nonce_hex` (0 to 255), `ticket_hex` (1 to 65535), `extensions` |
| 24 | `request_update` (0 or 1) |
| 12 | `curve_type` (3), `named_group`, `public_hex` (1 to 255 bytes), `algorithm`, `signature_hex` (0 to 65535) |
| 16 | `public_hex` (1 to 255 bytes) |
| 0, 14 | no fields (empty body) |

### Extension

Every extension object has `type` (uint16). A decoded extension adds the fields of its form; any other is `{type, extension_data_hex}` with the raw `extension_data`.

| Type | Name | Where | Form |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | server_name | ClientHello | `host_name`: exactly one entry of name_type 0 whose name is 1 to 65535 bytes of 0x21 to 0x7E, not ending in `.` |
| 0 | server_name | any other message | no fields: `extension_data` MUST be empty |
| 10 | supported_groups | any | `named_group_list`: non-empty list of uint16 |
| 11 | ec_point_formats | any | `ec_point_format_list_hex`: 1 to 255 bytes |
| 13 | signature_algorithms | any | `supported_signature_algorithms`: non-empty list of uint16 |
| 16 | application_layer_protocol_negotiation | ClientHello | `protocol_name_list_hex`: non-empty list of 1 to 255-byte names |
| 16 | application_layer_protocol_negotiation | other messages | the same field with exactly one name |
| 23 | extended_master_secret | any | no fields: `extension_data` MUST be empty |
| 43 | supported_versions | ClientHello | `versions`: list of uint16, 1 to 127 entries |
| 43 | supported_versions | ServerHello, HelloRetryRequest | `selected_version`: one uint16 |
| 44 | cookie | any | `cookie_hex`: 1 to 65535 bytes |
| 51 | key_share | ClientHello | `client_shares`: list (possibly empty) of `{group, key_exchange_hex (1 to 65535 bytes)}` with distinct groups |
| 51 | key_share | ServerHello | `server_share`: one `{group, key_exchange_hex}` |
| 51 | key_share | HelloRetryRequest | `selected_group`: one uint16 |
| 65281 | renegotiation_info | any | `renegotiated_connection_hex`: 0 to 255 bytes |

In a TLS 1.2 ServerHello only types 0, 11, 16, 23 and 65281 are decoded; others are kept raw.

### Where TLS 1.3 extensions may appear

The RFC 8446 section 4.2 table, extended with the TLS 1.2 extensions this codec decodes (11, 23, 65281: ClientHello only). CH ClientHello, SH ServerHello, HRR HelloRetryRequest, EE EncryptedExtensions, CT Certificate entry, CR CertificateRequest, NST NewSessionTicket:

| Types | Allowed in |
|---|---|
| 0, 1, 10, 14, 15, 16, 19, 20, 28 | CH, EE |
| 5, 18 | CH, CR, CT |
| 13, 47, 50 | CH, CR |
| 21, 45, 49, 11, 23, 65281 | CH |
| 41 | CH, SH |
| 42 | CH, EE, NST |
| 43 | CH, SH, HRR |
| 44 | CH, HRR |
| 48 | CR |
| 51 | CH, SH, HRR |

A type in this table, or one of the decoded types, found in a message the table does not list is `IllegalParameter`. These rules apply to the ClientHello, a HelloRetryRequest, a ServerHello that carries supported_versions, and every TLS 1.3-only message; types not in the table are carried raw anywhere.

## Functions

### decode_handshake

```pseudocode
decode_handshake(protocol: String, message: Bytes) -> HandshakeMessage | CodecError
```

**Algorithm:**

1. If `message` is shorter than 4 bytes, or `uint24(message[1..4]) != length(message) - 4`, return `DecodeError`.
2. If `message[0]` is not a type of `protocol`, return `UnexpectedMessage`.
3. Parse the body left to right. Every vector length is read from its length prefix and MUST lie in the range of the tables; a prefix that runs past its enclosing data, a range violation, or bytes left over at the end of the body or of any vector, is `DecodeError`.
4. A ServerHello whose `random` equals `CF 21 AD 74 E5 9A 61 11 BE 1D 8C 02 1E 65 B8 91 C2 A2 11 16 7A BB 8C 5E 07 9E 09 E2 C8 A8 33 9C` is a HelloRetryRequest; its extensions use the HRR forms and rules. Otherwise a ServerHello whose extension block contains type 43 uses the TLS 1.3 SH rules, and one without type 43 is a TLS 1.2 ServerHello.
5. Extensions are parsed as a list of `(type, data)` first; the whole block must parse. Then each, in order: a type already seen is `IllegalParameter`; a TLS 1.3 placement violation is `IllegalParameter`; then its data is decoded by its form (`DecodeError` on any violation, except that a ClientHello key_share listing a group twice is `IllegalParameter`, RFC 8446 section 4.2.8). The first failure in wire order is returned.
6. A ServerKeyExchange whose `curve_type` is not 3 (named_curve) is `IllegalParameter` as soon as that byte is read; the rest of an explicit-curve message has another format.
7. After the whole body has parsed: a ServerHello or HelloRetryRequest whose supported_versions selects a version other than 0x0304 is `IllegalParameter` (RFC 8446 section 4.2.1); a KeyUpdate whose `request_update` is not 0 or 1 is `IllegalParameter` (RFC 8446 section 4.6.3); a TLS 1.3 CertificateRequest without signature_algorithms is `MissingExtension` (section 4.3.2).

### encode_handshake

```pseudocode
encode_handshake(message: HandshakeMessage) -> Bytes
```

Writes the fields in wire order with minimal-width length prefixes as RFC 8446 and RFC 5246 define them, and the 4-byte header. Extensions are written in list order; raw ones as given. A ClientHello or ServerHello with `extensions: null` ends after its last fixed field; with an empty list it ends with a zero-length block. It performs no validation: encoding a message that does not decode is a caller error.

## Behavioral Contracts

**MUST:**

1. MUST decode every message of the tables and reject, with the listed error, every message that violates them; MUST NOT accept a message by ignoring trailing data.
2. MUST report the first failure in wire order, except the checks of step 7, which run after the body has parsed.
3. MUST keep unknown extensions, in order, with their exact bytes, so that a transcript can be re-encoded byte for byte.
4. MUST round-trip: `encode_handshake(decode_handshake(p, m)) == m`.
5. MUST NOT interpret `legacy_version`, the compression methods, the cipher suites or the groups; those are handshake decisions.

## Test Vectors

`decode_handshake` takes `protocol` and `message_hex` and returns the message object or an error. `encode_handshake` takes `message` (a message object) and returns `result_hex`. Every decode success also holds as an encode vector in reverse.

### Sources

- `rfc8448` vectors (20) decode the handshake messages printed in RFC 8448: ClientHello (with and without PSK and cookie), ServerHello and HelloRetryRequest, EncryptedExtensions, Certificate (RSA and ECDSA), CertificateRequest, CertificateVerify, Finished and NewSessionTicket.
- `openssl` vectors (14) decode messages OpenSSL 3.0.13 (the `ssl` module of Python 3.11.9, memory BIOs) produced: its ClientHello (a TLS 1.3 offer and a TLS 1.2-only offer), its TLS 1.3 ServerHello, its TLS 1.2 server flights (ServerHello, Certificate, ServerKeyExchange signed with ECDSA and with RSA-PSS, ServerHelloDone) and its ClientKeyExchange.
- `generated` vectors (81) are the reference client's ClientHello, the reference TLS 1.2 server's messages, short messages built by hand, the `encode_handshake` vectors, and the errors, each a single defect in an otherwise valid message.
- Every `decode_handshake` success was re-encoded and compared byte for byte. Every vector was re-checked from this file by `check_specs.py` twice: with the pure-Python primitives (`purecore.py`: HMAC, HKDF, AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305, X25519, P-256, ECDSA, RSA, Ed25519, written from their standards) and with pyca/cryptography 50.0.2 primitives under the same TLS logic. Both runs reproduce every expected value.

## Edge Cases

- **ClientHello without extensions** decodes with `extensions: null` (legal in TLS 1.2; a TLS 1.3 server then finds no supported_versions).
- **An empty extension block** (`00 00`) decodes to `[]` and re-encodes as `00 00`.
- **Empty key_share list** in a ClientHello is legal; it asks for a HelloRetryRequest.
- **Empty Certificate list** decodes; the handshake specs reject it.
- **GREASE values** (RFC 8701) are unknown extensions, groups and suites; they decode raw and are never errors here.
- **server_name in EncryptedExtensions** must be empty; a non-empty one is `DecodeError`.
- **An empty CertificateVerify signature** decodes; verification fails later.

## Implementation Notes

- **Bounded reads.** Parse each vector with a sub-reader limited to its length so an inner length cannot read past it.
- **Two passes for extensions.** Split the block into `(type, data)` first; then apply duplicate and placement checks and decode each.
- **Keep the raw bytes.** The transcript hash needs the message as received; never re-encode a received message to hash it.

## References

- [RFC 8446](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8446.html) -- handshake messages (4), extensions and their placement (4.2), HelloRetryRequest (4.1.4), KeyUpdate (4.6.3).
- [RFC 5246](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5246.html) -- TLS 1.2 messages (7.4).
- [RFC 8422](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8422.html) -- ServerKeyExchange and ClientKeyExchange for ECDHE (5.4, 5.7), ec_point_formats (5.1.2).
- [RFC 6066](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6066.html), [RFC 7301](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7301.html), [RFC 7627](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7627.html), [RFC 5746](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5746.html) -- server_name, ALPN, extended_master_secret, renegotiation_info.
- [RFC 8448](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8448.html) -- complete TLS 1.3 messages.
